text:
Mason Marchment scored the 100th goal of his NHL career on Wednesday against Pittsburgh, a tying goal for a player who went undrafted and spent years earning a spot. He signed a five-year deal in San Jose on July 1, a homecoming of sorts: his late father Bryan played six seasons for the Sharks.

The season itself has been quieter than the contract hoped. Eight points in 21 games, five goals right in line with his chances (4.8 expected goals). His scoring rate per hour is well under what our numbers expect, and part of that is bad luck: the Sharks have scored 5.1 fewer goals than the chances deserve with him on the ice.

The bigger issue is the team around him. San Jose gets only 41% of the expected goals with him out there at five on five, and the Sharks lost seven of eight games before the November 9 win over the Islanders. He's playing more, over 17 minutes in his last ten, and filling in on the top power-play unit when needed. The points should come as the luck evens out.
headline: Marchment hits 100, and the Sharks need more
